topic: What interference mitigation techniques are viable for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations?
consensus_response: For overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations, viable interference mitigation techniques include Analog Beamforming (ABF) to dynamically adjust antenna patterns and minimize co-channel interference. Rate Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) separates signals from different transmitters to reduce mutual interference. Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request (HARQ) improves reliability in error-prone channels by retransmitting packets with corrected errors. These techniques leverage the unique characteristics of satellite communications, such as multicast/broadcast functionality, to mitigate interference and ensure seamless coverage.
